# Russian sentences with the stress of every word written down: the truth the stress eval measures Speachy against.
# One sentence on a line.
#
# The rules:
#   1. A word is a run of Russian letters. A hyphen separates two words (по-пре́жнему is "по" and "пре́жнему").
#   2. Every word with two or more vowels shows where its stress is: U+0301 after the stressed vowel.
#   3. A word with ё carries no mark, because ё is the stress, unless its stress is elsewhere (трёхэта́жный).
#   4. A word that educated speakers say both ways carries both marks (заржа́ве́л): either is right.
#   5. A word with one vowel carries no mark.
#      A word that gives its stress to the word before it (не́ было, за́ руку) is marked as it is said alone
#      (бы́ло, ру́ку): the mark says which of the word's own vowels may be stressed.
#   6. ё is written wherever it is said, also where the source printed е. With the marks taken out, and ё kept,
#      a line is otherwise the sentence as it was printed: digits and abbreviations stay as they were.
#      No sentence occurs twice (compared with the marks taken out).
#   7. No Latin letters.
#
# Who placed the marks. An AI model placed them; no native speaker has checked this file. Where the dictionary
# Speachy itself marks from gives a word one stress, the mark was drafted from the dictionary and then read in its
# sentence and corrected where the dictionary was wrong for that sentence. Every other word (a word read two ways,
# a name, a word the dictionary lacks, a word said both ways, е or ё) was decided from the meaning of the sentence.
# Those hand-decided words, 141 of them, are listed for the owner's review in the pull request that added
# this file. The FLEURS lines were also compared with what a stress recognizer heard in 200 recordings of people
# reading them; the words it heard on another vowel were looked at one by one.
# A sentence with a name or a word whose stress could not be established with confidence was left out.
#
# Sources:
#   the first 108   FLEURS, Russian, dev split (Conneau et al., 2022), CC BY 4.0. The wording is the corpus's,
#                   mistakes included; only ё was restored.
#   the other 58    written for Speachy in the style of the articles its users select: news, science,
#                   technology, economics, culture; some with numbers, units and abbreviations.
#   The dictionary: RUAccent (MIT), the same one Speachy's stress table is built from.
